Each alphabet is kept as **one motif**: the whole sheet as it is drawn in the book, letters,
numbers, frames and small figures together. It is not split into letters here. To use an
alphabet as a font file, go to [Sjónabókarstafróf](https://github.com/HiDefTextiles/Sjonabok-stafrof),
which turns the same charts into TrueType fonts you can install and type with
([font gallery](https://hideftextiles.github.io/Sjonabok-stafrof/)).

```{=html}
<div id="alphabets" class="alphabets">
<ul class="nav nav-tabs" id="alpha-tabs" role="tablist"></ul>
<div class="tab-content" id="alpha-panes"><p class="count">Loading alphabets…</p></div>
</div>
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## How the tabs are chosen

The tabs come from one small table, [`gallery/regions.csv`](https://github.com/HiDefTextiles/Sjonabok/blob/main/gallery/regions.csv):
one row per tab, in order, with the countries it holds. Iceland is its own tab; every other
country falls under mainland Europe until that row is split into more countries. The same table
names the Collection filter in the [gallery](index.html). Which alphabet sheets have a font is
listed in [`patterns/alphabets/alphabets.csv`](https://github.com/HiDefTextiles/Sjonabok/blob/main/patterns/alphabets/alphabets.csv).
:::
